title: Jobs Shock, Bank Buyback Boom & AI Talent Wars - The Friday Market Wrap!
summary: The July 3 wrap favors banks as regulation becomes less restrictive and rejects a simple dollar-collapse narrative. Eisman explains risk-weighted capital and repo funding, offers a low-cut Fed outlook, and revisits AIG. Useful balance-sheet intuition is mixed with several categorical overstatements.
assessment: Bank resilience is supported by the 2025 stress tests. The forecast of at most two standard cuts in 2025 missed the eventual 75-basis-point easing. His repo-collateral definition and claim that this was the first friendly regulatory period since the GFC are incorrect.
framework_points: Analyze regulatory capital as a constraint on distributions and growth.
Distinguish dollar exchange-rate moves from reserve-currency infrastructure.
Investigate decentralized balance-sheet risk and unreliable accounting.
Keep management admiration separate from audited evidence.
transcript_cautions: June jobs were preliminary and later revised; the Fed forecasts are evaluated from what he said then.
Claims about AIG personal trading profits and management systems are recollections, not audited performance.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: Strong June jobs mean there will be no Fed cut this summer.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use the July and September decisions and preserve the ambiguous word summer.
claims.reason: There was no July cut, but the Fed cut September 17. That is after meteorological summer but before the autumn equinox, so the colloquial endpoint is ambiguous.

evidence.title: July 2025 FOMC decision
evidence.finding: The FOMC held the target range at 4.25%-4.50%.

evidence.title: September 2025 FOMC decision
evidence.finding: The FOMC cut the target range by 25 basis points to 4.00%-4.25%.

claims.next_check: Use the July and September decisions and preserve the ambiguous word summer.

claims.claim: Long Treasury yields have lacked a durable direction since late 2022.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Define maturity, endpoints and trend measure.
claims.reason: No range, trend measure or return convention is given. This is a descriptive market impression rather than a precise rate forecast.
claims.next_check: Define maturity, endpoints and trend measure.

claims.claim: Large compensation offers for AI researchers indicate that AI competition remains early and intense.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare hiring costs, capabilities and commercial outcomes.
claims.reason: Compensation can signal scarcity and competition, but does not establish the age or future returns of the investment cycle.
claims.next_check: Compare hiring costs, capabilities and commercial outcomes.

claims.claim: Apple cannot rapidly replace its China manufacturing ecosystem, and China may obstruct the transfer of expertise to India.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track assembly shares, supplier depth and primary regulatory actions.
claims.reason: The strategic dependence thesis requires product-specific production shares and documented restrictions. Reported engineer recalls alone do not establish government intent.
claims.next_check: Track assembly shares, supplier depth and primary regulatory actions.

claims.claim: Risk-weighted capital and stress losses help determine how much equity banks must retain.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile CET1, RWA, stress buffers and other binding limits.
claims.reason: The Fed stress-test framework uses projected capital losses against regulatory requirements. This is a simplified account, not the complete set of leverage, surcharge and liquidity constraints.

evidence.title: 2025 large-bank stress-test results
evidence.finding: All 22 tested banks stayed above minimum capital requirements under the severe hypothetical scenario. This supports resilience without proving immunity to every shock.

claims.next_check: Reconcile CET1, RWA, stress buffers and other binding limits.

claims.claim: Ever more severe stress scenarios can make banking uneconomic.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare modeled losses, binding capital and the cost of equity under defined scenarios.
claims.reason: This is a conditional policy argument without a specified scenario or required return threshold.
claims.next_check: Compare modeled losses, binding capital and the cost of equity under defined scenarios.

claims.claim: The 2025 stress results and regulatory shift favor greater bank capital returns.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track finalized buffers, authorized distributions and actual capital ratios.
claims.reason: The results showed all tested firms above minimum requirements and lower aggregate stressed losses than the preceding test. This supports capacity, but does not prove every bank should distribute all apparent excess.

evidence.title: 2025 large-bank stress-test results
evidence.finding: All 22 tested banks stayed above minimum capital requirements under the severe hypothetical scenario. This supports resilience without proving immunity to every shock.

claims.next_check: Track finalized buffers, authorized distributions and actual capital ratios.

claims.claim: Bowman personal recognition of excess regulation explains the favorable 2025 stress outcome.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare scenario design dates, model revisions and documented policy decisions.
claims.reason: The test design and supervisory models predate parts of the leadership transition. The transcript provides no counterfactual separating her influence from model and portfolio changes.
claims.next_check: Compare scenario design dates, model revisions and documented policy decisions.

claims.claim: This is the first period of bank-friendly regulation since the financial crisis.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare dated rule changes across administrations.
claims.reason: The 2018 relief legislation and 2019 tailoring rules are clear prior examples of relaxation. The degree and beneficiaries may differ, but first is incorrect.

evidence.title: 2019 tailoring rules
evidence.finding: The Fed had already tailored capital, liquidity and stress-testing requirements after the 2018 relief legislation. Regulatory relaxation was not new in 2025.

claims.next_check: Compare dated rule changes across administrations.

claims.claim: Regulatory easing will not restore the extreme leverage of the pre-GFC system.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track risk-based and simple leverage ratios through an explicitly defined policy period.
claims.reason: No future leverage threshold or time limit is supplied. The 2025 tests show current resilience rather than permanently constraining future policy.
claims.next_check: Track risk-based and simple leverage ratios through an explicitly defined policy period.

claims.claim: Powell may make zero, one or two cuts in 2025, rather than a large easing cycle.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the year-end target range with the July range.
claims.reason: The policy range fell 75 basis points from July through December, beyond two standard 25-basis-point cuts. The tentative wording reduces confidence but does not change the missed stated range.

evidence.title: July 2025 FOMC decision
evidence.finding: The FOMC held the target range at 4.25%-4.50%.

evidence.title: December 2025 FOMC decision
evidence.finding: The target range was cut to 3.50%-3.75%, 75 basis points below the July range, rather than at most two standard quarter-point cuts.

claims.next_check: Compare the year-end target range with the July range.

claims.claim: REIT stocks need major rate cuts to become attractive because investors own them for yield.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Model total returns from cash flow, financing and valuation as well as dividends.
claims.reason: The preference has no sector benchmark or return horizon and understates differences in rents, growth, leverage and cap rates. It cannot be treated as a precise short forecast.
claims.next_check: Model total returns from cash flow, financing and valuation as well as dividends.

claims.claim: A weaker dollar does not mean the dollar is about to lose its central international role.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track reserve shares, invoicing and funding alongside the exchange rate.
claims.reason: The Fed documents continued dominance in reserves, trade and funding. Exchange-rate depreciation and international monetary usage are different measurements.

evidence.title: International role of the dollar, 2025 edition
evidence.finding: The Fed documents continued dollar dominance across reserves, trade and funding, supported by deep US markets. Dominance does not imply permanent immunity to fiscal or political risks.

claims.next_check: Track reserve shares, invoicing and funding alongside the exchange rate.

claims.claim: Treasury market depth and its collateral role create a major obstacle to replacing the dollar.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare market depth, legal infrastructure and collateral usage across alternatives.
claims.reason: The Fed and New York Fed describe the institutional depth and collateral function supporting dollar use. This is a structural explanation, not proof that diversification cannot occur.

evidence.title: International role of the dollar, 2025 edition
evidence.finding: The Fed documents continued dollar dominance across reserves, trade and funding, supported by deep US markets. Dominance does not imply permanent immunity to fiscal or political risks.

evidence.title: Repo operation FAQs
evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
evidence.finding: Eligible collateral includes Treasury securities, agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities. Short funding tenor does not imply short maturity of all collateral.

claims.next_check: Compare market depth, legal infrastructure and collateral usage across alternatives.

claims.claim: Repo funding relies exclusively on short-term Treasury securities.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Inspect collateral schedules and distinguish loan tenor from collateral duration.
claims.reason: The New York Fed accepts Treasury, agency debt and agency MBS collateral. The maturity of a repo loan is distinct from the maturity of the pledged asset.

evidence.title: Repo operation FAQs
evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
evidence.finding: Eligible collateral includes Treasury securities, agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities. Short funding tenor does not imply short maturity of all collateral.

claims.next_check: Inspect collateral schedules and distinguish loan tenor from collateral duration.

claims.claim: US deficits are not an immediate financing problem because there is no comparable replacement currency.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track debt-service costs, term premiums and auction demand rather than require complete currency replacement.
claims.reason: Reserve demand can support financing, but it does not determine the yield at which debt clears or eliminate fiscal sensitivity. No threshold for a financing problem is given.
claims.next_check: Track debt-service costs, term premiums and auction demand rather than require complete currency replacement.

claims.claim: AIG accounting and governance deserved skepticism before the financial crisis.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use the documented transactions, restatements and settlement statement.
claims.reason: Greenberg later acknowledged involvement in transactions that inaccurately represented reserves and underwriting income. This supports specific accounting concerns, not every allegation or Eisman personal trading record.

evidence.title: Statement of Maurice R. Greenberg
evidence.finding: In settling the case, Greenberg acknowledged knowing involvement in two transactions that inaccurately portrayed AIG reserves and underwriting income, later restated in 2005.

claims.next_check: Use the documented transactions, restatements and settlement statement.

claims.claim: Decentralized risk control allowed AIG Financial Products to build dangerous exposures before the crisis.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Trace subsidiary exposures, collateral obligations and consolidated liquidity.
claims.reason: The FCIC documents the growth of AIG derivative exposure and failures of oversight. Other exposures, including securities lending, also mattered.

evidence.title: Financial Crisis Inquiry Report, findings and chapters 4, 6, 7, 13
evidence.finding: Investigative evidence documents fragile leverage/funding, fee and ROE incentives, deteriorating underwriting, and securitization dependence. Pages 61-64 describe pay incentives; pages 89 and 125 describe the origination chain; page 281 reports Bear near 38:1 and balance-sheet window dressing. Findings are not proof of a single exclusive cause.

claims.next_check: Trace subsidiary exposures, collateral obligations and consolidated liquidity.
